g.text: LOCK IT
Win+L / log out,
screens angled!
STRONG + MFA
long passphrases,
never shared!
NO PHISH
verify senders,
no odd links!
PERSONAL PHONES
no chart photos,
no USB patient data!
BREACH? STOP!
contain + report +
document — fast!
5 HABITS: lock screens + strong unique passwords/MFA + verify-before-click + clean
devices/USB discipline + breach response rehearsed. 90% of breaches start with a human click.
PASSWORDS: long passphrases ("koko!7am:wardB"), unique per system, changed per policy, NEVER
shared/taped/emailed. MFA on everything offered. Shared ward logins? Refuse + report — one
login per nurse, always (M02's rule!).
PHISHING: "urgent: verify your LHIMS password" + odd link = TRAP. Check sender address,
hover links, never open ward-system "updates" from email, report to IT, warn colleagues.
Ransomware enters through ONE click — then wards go paper for weeks.
PHONES + USB: no patient photos on personal phones (EVER — dismissal + prosecution!); no
records on unencrypted USB; ward WhatsApp = minimum info, consent, no full names/faces;
lost device = report IMMEDIATELY for remote wipe.
BREACH DRILL (exam list!): 1 CONTAIN (unplug? lock? retrieve printout?) · 2 REPORT (supervisor
+ IT + data officer, SAME shift) · 3 ASSESS (whose data? how many? harm?) · 4 NOTIFY (patients
+ Commission per policy) · 5 LEARN (root cause, fix, re-train). Cover-ups compound guilt.
SNOOPING PRICE: audit trails catch every view — curiosity clicks bring queries, suspension,
N&MC referral, dismissal. "Just checking on my auntie" is still a breach — visit, don't snoop.
LINKS: PRO-I M6 accountability · M02 audit trails · M06 social media perils.
MANTRA: "lock it, verify it, report it — my click is the firewall."
